title: Places and directions
subtitle: Maps, plans and landmarks
summary: Read a map before the recording starts, follow spoken directions, and use landmarks to place an answer on a plan.

media.label: Track 16
media.title: Four locations, four maps
media.caption: A gift shop, a stamp counter, a bridge and a frog's habitat. Listen for the landmark in each.

media.label: Track 17
media.title: Directions to the supermarket
media.caption: Three street plans, one set of directions. Trace the route as you listen.

media.label: Track 18
media.title: Brookside Market
media.caption: A map-labelling task with six options and only four answers.

lesson.heading: Study the map before you listen
lesson.text: You get reading time for a reason. Look at the map or plan and build a picture of it in your head: what is it a map of, what is already labelled, where is the entrance, what is in the centre. A clear image makes the spoken directions easy to follow.

examples.text: What is it a map of? **A market.**
Name three landmarks. **A tree, a fountain, a play area.**
Where is the entrance? **At the bottom, on the left.**
What is in the centre? **A tree.**

lesson.note: Features already printed on the map are the landmarks the speaker will use to guide you.

lesson.heading: Listen for the landmark, then the relation
lesson.text: A location is almost always given as a **landmark** plus a **relation** to it. Catch the landmark first - it is usually a word printed on your map - then listen for the little phrase that places the answer against it.

examples.text: The entrance is over there on your left. Then go straight ahead. The shop you want is **opposite the toilets**, next to the lifts.
In the middle of the resort you'll see a **circular courtyard**. To the right of the courtyard, you'll find a ... It's just behind the tree.
I was thinking of putting it right in the middle, but I think it would be better if it's at the **eastern end of the motorway**.
It is unable to live in the area of a pond ... it does need to live in fairly close proximity to water ... in a tiny burrow **surrounded by bushes**.

lesson.heading: The phrases that place things
rows: beside, alongside, adjacent to, right by
across from, facing, on the other side of
at the back of, just behind, in front of
in the middle of, halfway along, in between
at the northern end, on the eastern side, to the south of
close to, in close proximity to, not far from

lesson.heading: Two ways the task is set

left.label: Following directions
left.text: You are walked through a route step by step.
examples: *We're in Bridge Street now and it's in Queens Road.*
*You need to go up Bridge Street as far as the traffic lights, then turn right.*
*Then you walk along there to the next set of traffic lights and you'll be at Queens Road. You turn left there and it's the second shop on your left.*

right.label: Labelling a map
right.text: You match a list of options to numbered points.
examples: Read the option list several times before you start.
The options come in random order.
Do not cross an option out unless you are sure it is wrong.

lesson.note: Marking the route directly on the map as you listen is allowed, and it stops you losing your place.

lesson.heading: Distractors on a map
lesson.text: The extra options are not random. They are things that *are* at the market or on the plan, but not where the question asks - or things that have changed.

examples.note: Entry is complimentary now, so there is no need to pay - *complimentary* means free.
There are no books or second-hand goods for sale.

lesson.text: If you cannot decide between two answers, write both and move on. You can choose between them in the 10 minutes you get at the end - but only if you are still with the recording.

exercises.prompt: You hear *The shop you want is opposite the toilets, next to the lifts.* Which two words on the map are the landmarks?
exercises.explanation: The landmarks are the features already printed on your map. *Opposite* and *next to* are the relations that place the answer against them.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase with what it means on a map.

pairs.right: on the right, if north is up
further from you than the tree

exercises.statement: You should cross out options on a map-labelling task as soon as you think they might be wrong.
exercises.explanation: Only cross out an option when you are sure. An early guess can remove the answer you need two questions later.

exercises.prompt: *Entry is ___ now, so there's no need to pay.* The word means *free*.
exercises.explanation: This is exactly why *ticket booth* was a distractor - the booth exists, but nobody buys a ticket.

exercises.prompt: Build the direction that gets you to Queens Road.
exercises.answer: You need to go up Bridge Street as far as the traffic lights, then turn right.
exercises.explanation: *As far as* gives you the stopping point; *then turn* gives you the change of direction.

exercises.prompt: Sort these into what they tell you.
Before the recording starts, what is the most useful thing to do with a map?
options: Copy it onto your answer sheet
Find the entrance and the printed landmarks, and picture the layout
Guess the answers so you can check them later
Count how many options there are and choose the middle one
exercises.explanation: Having a clear image in your mind is what lets you follow the directions in real time. You only hear them once.

exercises.statement: In a map task with options A-F and four questions, every option is used.
exercises.explanation: There are more options than questions, so some are never the answer - two of them at Brookside Market.

exercises.prompt: *I was thinking of putting it right in the middle, but I think it would be better if it's at the ___ end of the motorway.*
exercises.explanation: *I was thinking of* introduces the idea the speaker then changes - the middle is the distractor.

exercises.prompt: *It does need to live in fairly close proximity to water, but it is unable to live in the area of a pond.* Where does the animal live?
options: Near water, but not in the pond
exercises.explanation: *Close proximity to water* places it near; *unable to live in the area of a pond* rules the pond out. Both halves are needed.
